To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Na partitions to PbS precipitates in PbI(2) doped PbTe, and the segregation of Na at the PbTe/PbI(2) interface results in the formation of PbS precipitate with a faceted morphology.

1) Na segregates to PbTe/PbTe interfaces, 2) Na segregation at the interfaces lowers the interfacial energy and results in the formation of faceted PbS nanostructures, 3) Na is a good candidate for controlling morphological anisotropic of PbS nanostructures in a solid-state solution.

the addition of a ternary solute in a binary matrix/precipitates system can control the morphology of the precipitates, and that this is mediated by segregation of the solute to matrix-precipitate interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of phase separation in PbI(2) and Na doped PbTe.
the control of morphology and microstructure of nano- and microstructures.
the development and application of novel nanoscale materials for thermoelectric power generation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of Na to the PbI(2) doped PbTe-Pbs system results in Na partitioning to the precipitates (PbS) and segregating at the precipitate/matrix (PbTe) interfaces.

the addition of sodium to the PbTe matrix results in a significant decrease of the interfacial energy between the PbS and PbTe phases and a significant increase in the surface energy of the PbS phase.

the morphology of nanometer scale precipitates in a host matrix is determined by the partitioning of a solute element between the host matrix and the precipitate phase, and that this partitioning is governed by the energetics of the matrix/precitate interface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the morphology control of PbS precipitate in PbTe matrix is mediated by solute segregation of Na at the matrix/ precipitate interface, and this segregation is driven by the anisotropic interdiffusion of Na in the PbTe/PbTe and PbTe/PbSe interface.
we have demonstrated a new strategy for morphological control of nanostructures, mediated by segregation of a solute at the matrix/phase interface.
the morphology of PbS nanostructures in a PbTe-PbI(2) matrix can be controlled by the addition of Na as a solubilizing dopant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphological anisotropic behavior is driven by solute segregation and that the solute partitioning is a key parameter in determining the morphology.
the addition of a third element (Na) to PbS-PbTe system can alter the surface energies of PbS precipitate, resulting in a change in the PbS morphology.
a small amount of Na (1 mol %) in the matrix can control the morphology of PbS precipitate in PbTe, and this control is mediated by Na segregating to the PbTe/PbTe interfaces.
